rationale: Only untried model×prompt combo on the matrix. Baseline measured Sonnet with the vanilla composed_prompt (0.95 quality, 44687ms); current parent measures gpt-5-6-luna with the concise 1-2 sentence agent prompt (0.925 quality, 22904ms). Sonnet-with-concise is unmeasured. The concise prompt's explicit anti-pad directive ('do not introduce facts not in source') is exactly the summary_quality failure mode on short rules (2010, 2020) where fast models drift into FINRA knowledge from training; Sonnet's stronger instruction-following should realize the directive where gpt-5-6-luna doesn't. Latency math: Sonnet is decode-dominant on 10-section FINRA PDFs; the concise prompt halves expected output tokens vs the vanilla composed prompt that produced the 44687ms baseline, projecting ~22-30s median — inside the 24904ms upper bound (frontier 22904 + 2000 latency ε) in the plausible range. Expected outcome: quality 0.95→0.975 or 1.0 (upside crosses the 0.03 quality ε), latency ~25-30s (likely within 2000ms epsilon of frontier best). Clean single-step attribution: if quality moves >0.03 and latency ≤24904ms the frontier extends on quality; if latency slips just outside the epsilon window with 1.0 quality, next round compounds a size-router to shift the largest PDFs to gpt-5-6-luna. No no_repeat conflict: Sonnet has never been set via the lever and Sonnet+concise is an unmeasured combination; Round 4's anti-pad-directive-on-Haiku revert is a different model class.
